issues.description: Cardinality explosion: unbounded runtime values written into stats keys with no sanitization or cap
issues.detail: value_to_metric writes entry.Value verbatim into the metric key via WriteString(entry.Value). The runtime value is attacker- or client-controlled (route, user, action, etc.). There is no length cap, no allowed-character set, and no upper bound on distinct values. The resulting stats store will allocate a new counter struct per unique value, in the existing statsManager.NewStats map; this is a denial-of-service vector and an asymptotic memory-growth bug (O(distinct request values)). Knuth: the data-structure choice (an unbounded map keyed by client input) is wrong for this operation. At minimum: cap key length, restrict to a safe charset (replace '.', whitespace, control chars), document the cardinality risk in the same words as detailed_metric, and consider an LRU or explicit ceiling.

issues.description: Stats counter is created twice on every value_to_metric path; the first counter is orphaned
issues.detail: In the post-loop branch (lines ~419-430), the code calls NewRateLimit(... NewStats(rateLimit.FullKey) ...) and then immediately overwrites rateLimit.Stats with this.statsManager.NewStats(enhancedKey). That means every GetLimit call on a value_to_metric path allocates a fresh Stats object under the old key, registers its counters in the stats store, then discards it. This is both a correctness issue (ghost counters appearing under the non-enhanced key) and a steady leak of stats handles per request. The invariant 'one Stats per (rateLimit, key)' is violated. The fix is to build the enhanced key first and call NewStats once.

issues.description: rateLimit is reassigned to a fresh pointer inside GetLimit, breaking shared-state semantics for cached limits
issues.detail: rateLimit is obtained from nextDescriptor.limit (a pointer stored on the descriptor tree shared across requests). The new branch does `rateLimit = NewRateLimit(...)` which replaces the local pointer but the *returned* RateLimit is now a per-call object, while every other code path in this function returns the shared descriptor.limit pointer. Callers and tests that compare identity, mutate fields, or rely on the shared Stats across requests will see divergent behavior on value_to_metric paths vs. all other paths. More importantly, the per-request NewRateLimit means stats and limit state are no longer shared across requests for the same descriptor under value_to_metric — counters reset per call unless the stats store dedupes by name. State the invariant: 'GetLimit returns the descriptor's canonical RateLimit'; this code breaks it.

issues.description: Per-request strings.Builder allocations and per-request map lookups in stats store on hot path
issues.detail: GetLimit is called on every rate-limit request. The new code unconditionally allocates a second strings.Builder (valueToMetricFullKey) and writes to it for every entry of every descriptor, even when no descriptor in the config uses value_to_metric. Then, when the enhanced key differs from FullKey, it performs two statsManager.NewStats calls (which do a map lookup and possibly a counter registration). The complexity is unchanged asymptotically (O(entries)), but the constants are non-trivial on a high-QPS path. Knuth: measure before optimizing — but at least gate the second Builder behind a 'this subtree has any value_to_metric descriptor' boolean computed at load time, so the cost is zero for configs that don't use the feature.

issues.description: Loop invariant for valueToMetricFullKey is not stated and the three branches duplicate logic that should be one expression
issues.detail: The if/else if/else block at lines ~358-403 has three cases (matchedViaWildcard, matchedUsingValue, default), each of which reduces to: 'write key; if valueToMetric and value!='' then write _value'. The wildcard branch's behavior is identical to the default-key branch's valueToMetric==true sub-branch. The code reads like three independent paths but they collapse to one rule. State the invariant in a comment ('after this block, valueToMetricFullKey contains the metric segment for entry i: key, optionally suffixed _value when valueToMetric is set and value is non-empty'), then write it as one branch. This is exactly the literate-programming gap the lens exists to flag.

issues.description: valueToMetric flag is read from nextDescriptor (the matched child), not from prevDescriptor — semantics are subtle and undocumented
issues.detail: The flag affects how *this* level's segment is rendered, but it is read from nextDescriptor.valueToMetric (the child that was just matched). This is the correct intent (the flag belongs to the descriptor whose value is being rendered), but it interacts oddly when no child matches (nextDescriptor==nil), in which case the code falls through to writing just entry.Key with no value. The invariant for the no-match branch should be stated: 'if no descriptor matched, we cannot consult value_to_metric, so default to key-only'. Also note: there is no test for the case where value_to_metric is set on a descriptor whose value matches an explicit key+value with an empty configured Value — verify behavior.

issues.description: FullKey is referenced before it is reliably set on the non-detailed path
issues.detail: The post-loop block reads rateLimit.FullKey to compare against enhancedKey, but FullKey is only set in this function inside the new DetailedMetric branch (`rateLimit.FullKey = detailedKey`) or, presumably, at construction time. If a descriptor's RateLimit was created with FullKey == '' (the default), then `enhancedKey != rateLimit.FullKey` is trivially true on every value_to_metric==false request that happens to share the shared rateLimit, triggering the NewRateLimit/NewStats reallocation path for descriptors that never opted into value_to_metric. Verify NewRateLimit always populates FullKey to the non-enhanced default and that no descriptor in the tree starts with FullKey==''. This is the kind of off-by-one-in-state-machine bug the audit step exists to catch.

issues.description: No test covers the cardinality bound, key sanitization, or extreme inputs
issues.detail: Tests verify happy paths and the detailed_metric precedence rule but do not exercise: (a) a value containing '.', whitespace, or non-ASCII (which will corrupt the dotted metric namespace); (b) very long values; (c) high cardinality across many requests to confirm the stats store does not unboundedly grow. Knuth: tests catch what proofs miss — add at least one test that pins the intended sanitization behavior, even if that test is the one that fails and forces the sanitization to be written.

issues.description: Documentation under-states the cardinality risk that detailed_metric documents explicitly
issues.detail: The README for detailed_metric carries the warning 'this should only be enabled in situations where the potentially large cardinality of metrics that this can lead to is acceptable.' The new value_to_metric section omits that warning even though the feature has the same cardinality semantics (it embeds runtime values into metric names). Mirror the warning, and ideally note that values are not sanitized so '.' or whitespace in values will affect downstream metric backends.

review.summary: The feature is well-motivated and the YAML-plumbing portion is straightforward, but the GetLimit changes are under-audited at exactly the levels this lens cares about. Two correctness/state-management bugs stand out (double Stats allocation creating ghost counters under the old key, and replacing the shared per-descriptor RateLimit pointer with a per-request one), plus an unbounded-cardinality data-structure problem that mirrors detailed_metric's documented risk but without detailed_metric's warning. The new metric-building block also reads as three duplicated branches with an unstated invariant; collapsing them to one rule with a stated invariant would make the code literate and remove the place where the FullKey comparison subtly misbehaves. Add tests for sanitization and cardinality, gate the second Builder on a load-time 'any value_to_metric in subtree' flag, and rebuild stats exactly once. Decision: UNDER-AUDITED, with one WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE flag for the unbounded stats map keyed on raw runtime values.
